answer: Stakes sit in a mutual haven where each bond covers the others in its grove, and a fault found in one member slashes every bond in that grove at once, dropping the whole grove into a tundra where nothing earns. A farm of n clones carries n times the exposure of a lone agent on any single detection, so it buys cover from outside, and each outside underwriter covers one identity only and forfeits its own stake if that identity is found faulty, so cover can never be pooled across clones.
